approval: Same authorized C1 logical phase, with corrected strict parsing and carried remaining resources. Preserve both prior contracts and counted costs; see continuation.json.

budget.note: Remaining original logical-phase resources after five probe attempts and four builds. Planned 24 probe plus 84 fast guests; seven guest attempts remain for validity failures. Fresh correctness is required under the corrected parser. The shortened wall cap preserves the earlier R2 deadline.

wall_estimate.note: Remaining full correctness and traced workload have not been completed. Guest timeout remains 900 seconds; this contract has a shortened wall limit of 58398 seconds.

accelerator.kvm_default: run.py keeps KVM, 8 vCPU and 8192 MiB when SWAP_NEXT_ACCEL is unset. This revision's child environment sets SWAP_NEXT_ACCEL=tcg, SWAP_NEXT_TCG_SMP=4 and SWAP_NEXT_TCG_MEM_MIB=4096, and the workflow rejects any result whose accelerator is not tcg.
accelerator.host_cpus: This revision does not offline or online host CPUs.

backends.disk: 16 GiB preallocated virtio raw swap file, cache=none. 2 MiB THP policy is set; swap-in opts out with MADV_NOHUGEPAGE.
backends.zswap: lzo/zsmalloc, shrinker enabled, backed by lz4 zram1 20000M. Guest cmdline sets zswap.enabled=1 and zswap.compressor=lzo.
backends.zram: lz4 zram0 3200M priority 100 and zram1 20000M priority 0. Not a scored case.
backends.zram-64k: lz4 zram0 8G, 64 KiB THP only; retained swap-in regression guard.
backends.brd: 1 TiB brd (brd.rd_size=1073741824). Probe-only metadata case, plain mode, so SwapTotal is the brd device alone.
backends.compressed: XSwap virtual device only, with no lower physical swap backing. Nonzero compressible target data, pagemap/mincore residency, and one successful PID-filtered zswap_load return per timed touch; trace loss and misses invalidate the sample.

page_cluster.guest: bench.sh reads /proc/sys/vm/page-cluster, prints PAGE_CLUSTER, and fails unless the value is 3. It does not write the sysctl.

baseline_lineage.note: Build requested archive from the frozen object store; never change linux/ HEAD. Both compared arms use identical tracing-enabled common configuration.

guest_image.prepare: python3 benchmark/swap-standard/prepare-image.py --src <pinned valkey and vm-scalability checkouts> --busybox-template <busybox rootfs>
guest_image.where: Designated Linux worker; exact source, image and initramfs provenance is verified before each guest.
guest_image.contains: guest-init, bench.sh, params.sh, swapin, churn, correctness, console-drain, and the pinned linux source archive and compression

order: alternating AB then BA; same order in calibration

repetition.reclaim_target: At least 90% of each 64 MiB order for compressed; at least 90% of the 1 GiB region for disk/zram.

validity.host_load: loadavg and PSI when /proc/pressure exists, stored on every attempt before launch and after exit

screen: TCG exploratory C1 shared compression screen; compression primary and disk/zram guards. No slow tier or automatic code acceptance.

excluded.build: kbench build OOMs in a 470M memcg on this tree: the 2026-10-27 KVM smoke killed objtool after about 17 min with anon-rss 465668 kB and 445 MiB already swapped. BUILD_MEMCG stays 470M and BUILD_JOBS stays 32. This revision does not score build. A full TCG kernel build also does not fit guest_timeout 900s. The parser already records build_system_usec when a build guest runs; this revision never launches one, so system time is not a result.
excluded.usemem-rand: OOM and synchronization hang in the pre-kbench integration; not a case in this revision.

rejected_alternatives.raise_memcg: A limit that fits objtool abandons the kbench pressure point and still leaves a full kernel build, which does not finish inside guest_timeout under TCG.
rejected_alternatives.reduce_jobs: The killed task was objtool on vmlinux, which is not a -j fan-out. Reducing -j would also change the shared kbench parameter.

purpose: Test shared page/object compression as architecture preparation; preserve frontend behavior and resource/latency guards.
measurement_revision: Revision 8 adds complete hash-bound C1 configuration correctness and 128 MiB compressed-resident instrumented swap-in. Existing disk/zram use 1 GiB. Metadata retains revision 7 attributable accounting with fresh calibration; historical protocols and outcomes remain unchanged. This separately frozen contract replaces only the contradictory debug input with c1-debug-v2; all timing and correctness gates remain unchanged. Original C1 costs are deducted from its available resources. This continuation corrects recognition of the expected invalid-codec diagnostic and standard zero-skip KUnit summaries without changing semantic gates or timing. Prior raw outcomes remain failed; correctness is collected afresh.
ceiling_justification: The ceiling is 25%, the bottom of the 25-30% band used by revision 3 and the revision 4 template. Revision 2 TCG pair-median spreads were 4-10% and worst-pair tails were 19-28%. A 25% ceiling fails the tier as CALIBRATION_NOISY when the scored-mean p90 exceeds 25%, which stops candidate comparison until the measurement is cleaner. A 30% ceiling would accept noise as large as the effect the revision 3 screen was meant to resolve. There is no TCG kbench A/A yet; the first passing calibration's per-metric p90 is the observation that would support a later revision with a different ceiling. Confidence in applying the revision 3 split to this setup is medium.
mechanism_evidence: Exact-tree reviewed extraction and lifetime argument
Nonzero compressed objects and observed demand decode with no lower backing
Payload and zsmalloc backing observations plus static context/metadata footprint review
limitations: Compression latency includes probe execution cost; trace reads are outside the timed touch.
The 128 MiB total target splits into sequential and random halves; timed counts reflect verified initially swapped targets.
C1 preserves ZSwap policy and does not implement independent XSwap or tier migration.
A failed correctness matrix stops dependent execution. A noisy calibration prevents speed or equivalence claims.
KUnit source semantics require exact-tree independent review; accepted test names alone are insufficient.
No host CPU, swap or kernel changes. No slow tier or promotion.
